Apple has updated the privacy policy for its Apple Store app, adding terms related to an upcoming virtual shopping assistant. Details below.

Apple is expanding its use of artificial intelligence in retail operations

According to MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page have added a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," which reads as follows:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon feature a chatbot that delivers personalised responses based on user data and helps users make purchasing decisions.

Apple says it will strip out personally identifiable information before sharing conversations with an unnamed partner to generate assistant responses, suggesting that at least part of the experience is likely powered by a third-party model from an external company.

Chat history will be retained within the app for users to revisit, and will also be stored for Apple's business analytics purposes. Users can opt in or out of having their conversations used to improve the virtual shopping assistant via a new "Chat Improvements" setting.

Judging by the wording of Apple's privacy policy, the virtual assistant may initially launch only in select countries and regions, and could debut first in English-speaking markets before gradually expanding to more languages and regions.

This news comes several months after Apple added an AI chatbot to its Sales Coach app, providing Apple retail partners with sales and technical resources. Staff can access the chatbot via the "Ask" tab, which draws on official Apple training materials and documents to answer questions.

Separately, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple has been testing a system called "Live Notes" at certain retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing staff to focus on customers without being distracted by note-taking.
